author: baltinerdist
body:
## Summary

- **Split weekly and monthly attendance into separate queries.** `GetKingdomParkAverages` previously scanned `ork_attendance` twice in a single query — once for 26 weeks and once for 12 months. The monthly subquery has been extracted into a new `GetKingdomParkMonthlyAverages` function with its own independent 600 s cache, eliminating the double scan on page load.
- **Monthly column now loads asynchronously.** The kingdom index page renders immediately with weekly (Ave.) and Total columns populated synchronously. After `DOMContentLoaded`, a jQuery `$.get` fetches `Kingdom/park_monthly_json/{id}` and fills in the Monthly column without blocking page render.
- **Fixed a correctness bug in monthly grouping.** The old monthly subquery grouped by `date_month` (integer 1–12) without `date_year`, causing attendance records from the same calendar month in two different years (e.g. Feb 2025 and Feb 2026) to collapse into a single row. The new query groups by `date_year, date_month, mundane_id, park_id`, counting each year-month occurrence separately.
- **Removed an unnecessary `LEFT JOIN ork_mundane` from the weekly subquery.** That join is only needed when the `NativePopulace` or `Waivered` filter flags are active. For the kingdom index (which passes neither), the join was evaluated against every attendance row with no effect. It is now added conditionally.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `system/lib/ork3/class.Report.php` | `GetKingdomParkAverages` → weekly-only + conditional mundane JOIN; new `GetKingdomParkMonthlyAverages` |
| `orkservice/Report/ReportService.function.php` | Thin wrapper for new function |
| `orkservice/Report/ReportService.definitions.php` | WSDL type definitions for new function |
| `orkservice/Report/ReportService.registration.php` | SOAP registration for new function |
| `orkui/controller/controller.Kingdom.php` | New `park_monthly_json` action — returns `{park_id: monthly_count}` JSON and exits |
| `orkui/template/default/Kingdom_index.tpl` | Monthly cells use `—` placeholder + async jQuery fill; `data-park-id` added to park rows |

## Test plan

- [ ] Load a kingdom index page (e.g. `/orkui/index.php?Route=Kingdom/index/18`) and confirm it renders without delay — Ave. and Total columns should be populated immediately
- [ ] Confirm the Monthly column shows `—` briefly then populates with decimal values (e.g. `12.3`) after a short pause
- [ ] Open DevTools Network tab and confirm a second request to `Kingdom/park_monthly_json/18` returns valid JSON `{"123": 45, ...}`
- [ ] Verify the Monthly totals row also updates correctly
- [ ] Test a kingdom with `NativePopulace` or `Waivered` filters (via reports) to confirm the conditional mundane JOIN still works for those callers
- [ ] Clear the cache and reload to confirm both the weekly and monthly queries execute correctly from cold

author: timon0305
body:
## Purpose

Fix HTTP status code for requests that exceed the model's maximum context length. Currently, vLLM returns HTTP 400 (Bad Request) when input tokens exceed `max_model_len` or when `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens` is too large for the remaining context. According to [HTTP semantics](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status/413), HTTP 413 (Content Too Large) is the correct status code when the request entity exceeds server-defined limits.

Fixes #34340

### Changes

- Add `VLLMContentTooLargeError` exception subclass of `VLLMValidationError` in `vllm/exceptions.py`
- Map `VLLMContentTooLargeError` to HTTP 413 in `create_error_response()` (`engine/serving.py`)
- Use `VLLMContentTooLargeError` for all three token-limit violations in `_validate_input()`:
  - Input tokens exceeding `max_model_len` for embedding/score/classification requests
  - Input tokens >= `max_model_len` for completion requests
  - `max_tokens + input_tokens > max_model_len`
- Handle `VLLMContentTooLargeError` in `validation_exception_handler` (`server_utils.py`)
- Document HTTP 413 response in API router OpenAPI specs for chat completions, completions, and responses endpoints

author: bruno-garcia
body:
## Summary

Overhaul the enrichment pipeline to reduce API call volume by ~30-80x and add smarter prioritization. Also adds a new PR Explorer page.

**Before:** ~10.4M REST API calls, ~40+ days with 2 tokens
**After:** ~120-310K GraphQL queries, ~2-5 days (faster with more tokens)

## Changes

### Pipeline: eliminate waste
- **Reorder enrichment stages** to repos → comments → reactions → PRs (PRs deprioritized since no app page uses that data yet)
- **70% round-robin threshold**: skip stages above 70% complete so all data dimensions get enriched before any single stage finishes
- **Drop `repo_languages` fetching** — the app only uses `repos.primary_language`, never the `repo_languages` breakdown table. Saves 1 API call per repo (~387K calls)

### Pipeline: GraphQL batch enrichment
- **Repos** (`graphql-repos.ts`): 30 repos per query using field aliases. REST fallback on failure.
- **Comments** (`graphql-comments.ts`): 20 PRs per query using `reviewThreads` — naturally filters replies, includes reaction counts via `reactionGroups`.
- **Reactions** (`graphql-reactions.ts`): 50 PRs per query, checks hooray reactions with user info in a single call. Replaces 2-step REST flow (check count → fetch users).
- **PRs** (`graphql-pull-requests.ts`): 30 PRs per query with reactions via `reactionGroups`. Maps GraphQL `MERGED`/`CLOSED`/`OPEN` state enum.

All four modules follow the same pattern: `octokit.request("POST /graphql")` for header access, partial error handling, rate limiter integration, REST fallback.

### Pipeline: smarter ordering
- **Priority by recency + stars**: `ORDER BY latest_week DESC, repo_stars DESC` in comment, reaction, and PR enrichment queries. Joins `repos` table for star counts. Most valuable data enriched first.

### App: PR Explorer page
- New `/prs` page for browsing PRs reviewed by AI bots
- Sort by: most bots, thumbs up, comments, repo stars, most recent
- Filter by product
- Pagination matching the orgs page pattern
- Shows state badges, bot names, reaction counts, repo stars
- Added "PRs" to navigation

### Pipeline: BigQuery validation tool
- New `validate-bq-prs` CLI command comparing ClickHouse PR data against BigQuery
- Samples N enriched PRs, queries GH Archive for matching events, compares fields
- For future: determine if BigQuery could replace API calls for PR metadata

## Issues closed

Closes #85, closes #86, closes #87, closes #88, closes #89, closes #90, closes #91, closes #92, closes #93, closes #95

body:
# feat: Expand COBOL backend to professional banking system with Flask API and React frontend

## Summary

Expands the original 3-operation COBOL backend into a 15-operation professional banking system and adds a three-tier architecture: COBOL backend (1300+ lines), Flask REST API middleware, and React frontend.

**COBOL Backend** – expanded from `CREATE_ACCOUNT`, `CHECK_ACCOUNT`, `CALCULATE_SCORE` to 15 operations covering account CRUD, deposits/withdrawals/transfers, loan management (create, pay, check, list with amortization calculations), credit scoring, transaction history logging, and a dashboard summary. All output is JSON. Compiles and runs successfully against `data/input.dat`.

**Flask API** (`api/app.py`) – REST middleware that spawns the COBOL binary via `subprocess`. State persistence is achieved by maintaining an operations log (`api/.state/operations.log`): each request replays all prior mutating operations before appending the new one. Mutations are only persisted on `"status": "OK"` responses. A threading lock serializes access.

**React Frontend** (`frontend/`) – 5 pages: Dashboard, Accounts (CRUD + detail modal), Operations (deposit/withdraw/transfer), Loans (create/pay with amortization charts), Reports (credit score + transaction history). Clean, light-themed Revolut-style banking UI with sidebar navigation.

**Scripts** – `run-api.sh`, `run-frontend.sh`, `run-all.sh` added for full-stack startup.

## Updates since last revision

### UI Redesign – Revolut Aesthetic (Light Theme)
User requested replacing the previous dark YouTube-like theme with a design inspired by [Revolut](https://www.revolut.com/es-ES/). Changes:

- **Complete CSS rewrite** – light color scheme (`#ffffff` background, `#f7f7f7` page bg, `#0066ff` accent, `#191c1f` text), Inter font, clean minimalist layout
- **Pill-shaped buttons** – `border-radius: 999px` matching Revolut's button style
- **Card-based layout** – white cards with subtle `box-shadow` on light gray page background
- **Sidebar** – white background with black active-state highlighting, clean section headers
- **Tables** – light alternating rows, subtle borders, professional styling
- **Forms** – light gray input backgrounds (`#f7f7f7`) with blue focus rings
- **Tabs** – pill-shaped background tabs instead of border-based
- **Status badges** – soft colored backgrounds (green for active, red for errors, etc.)

Files changed: `index.css` (99% rewrite), `Accounts.js`, `Loans.js`, `Reports.js` (CSS class updates).

All existing functionality preserved: keyboard input, search/filter, loan amortization charts, CRUD operations, credit scoring visualization.

author: johanneslichtenberger
body:
## Summary

- Extracts PipeExpr compilation from the translator inheritance hierarchy into a pluggable `PipelineStrategy` interface, with `SequentialPipelineStrategy` (from `TopDownTranslator`) and `BlockPipelineStrategy` (from `BlockTranslator`) implementations
- Makes the execution model (sequential vs. parallel) orthogonal to store-specific translator customizations, allowing downstream translators like `SirixTranslator` to switch execution models without a new subclass
- Adapts `ProfilingCompiler` to use a custom strategy that preserves operator profiling behavior

## Test plan

- [x] All 952 tests pass (`mvn clean test`), including `ParallelExecutionTest` for block execution and all sequential query tests
- [x] No API changes to `CompileChain` or `BlockCompileChain` — they still create `TopDownTranslator` / `BlockTranslator` respectively

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core query compilation for `PipeExpr` and refactors how operator pipelines are built, so regressions could affect broad query execution paths despite largely being code motion/extraction.
> 
> **Overview**
> Refactors `PipeExpr` compilation to be strategy-driven via a new `PipelineStrategy` interface, making the execution model (sequential vs block/parallel) configurable without changing translator subclasses.
> 
> Introduces `SequentialPipelineStrategy` (extracted from `TopDownTranslator`) and `BlockPipelineStrategy` (extracted from `BlockTranslator`), updates `Compiler` to delegate `XQ.PipeExpr` to the injected strategy, and simplifies `TopDownTranslator`/`BlockTranslator` to primarily select/configure the appropriate strategy (including preserving the `parallel`/`ordered` behavior).
> 
> Updates `ProfilingCompiler` to use a custom strategy that wraps operator compilation in `ProfileOperator` nodes so operator profiling continues to work under the new delegation model.
>

author: alexzhang13
body:
Compaction (off by default): Root history is stored in the REPL history variable. When usage reaches a configurable percentage of the model’s context limit, the run is summarized, the summary is appended to history, and the loop continues from that summary. System prompt updated to mention history.

Token-based threshold: Compaction uses a percentage of context (default 85%). Added `rlm.utils.token_utils`: model context limits (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, gpt-5, gpt-5-nano), containment-based model matching, and token counting (tiktoken when available, else ~4 chars/token).

FINAL_VAR: When FINAL_VAR is run inside a REPL block, its value is stored on the execution result and used as the final answer by the main loop (no second execution). Support FINAL_VAR with a direct value (e.g. FINAL_VAR(result) where result is an int). Treat “variable not found” as non-final so the loop can continue; use only stdout for the final answer.
Verbose: Log when compaction runs and, each step, log current tokens vs compaction threshold.

## Summary

## Type of Change

The `ajv@6.12.6` vulnerability ([GHSA-2g4f-4pwh-qvx6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g4f-4pwh-qvx6)) is a ReDoS issue in a transitive dependency of ESLint. Key facts:
- ESLint is a dev dependency — not shipped to users
- No fix available upstream (ajv 6.x won't be patched)
- The vulnerability requires attacker-controlled input to exploit
- In a dev tool context, this is extremely low risk

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a configuration-equivalent way to reproduce Inkscape Trace Bitmap (Multicolor) controls (Scans/Colors, Speckles, Smooth corners, Optimize) inside the in-browser raster→vector pipeline. 
- Let users tune tracing using the same conceptual parameters so outputs are closer to what Inkscape produces while keeping the existing max-8-color limit.

### Description
- Added explicit trace tuning constants and exposed them in the analysis settings: `traceSpeckles`, `traceSmoothCorners`, and `traceOptimize` in `assets/js/threaddesk.js`.

- Updated `smoothClosedLoopPath(points)` to drive corner rounding from `traceSmoothCorners` and produce quadratic curve segments instead of hard-corner runs.
- Rewrote the vector-path builder to assemble loops per label, filter speckle loops by area using `traceSpeckles`, and apply `traceOptimize` when simplifying contours, then emit filled paths with `fill-rule="evenodd"`.

author: derealizacjaaa
body:
## Summary
This PR adds a complete, production-ready R implementation of the Directed Batch Growing Self-Organizing Map (DBGSOM) algorithm based on Vasighi & Amini (2017). The implementation includes the core SOM training algorithm, dynamic hexagonal grid growth, NA-aware distance metrics, quality metrics, clustering, and visualization support.

## Key Changes

### Core Algorithm Implementation
- **dbgsom.R**: Main class constructor, two-phase training (coarse with growth, fine without), predict, and transform methods
- **topology.R**: Hexagonal grid topology using odd-r offset coordinates with 6-connected neighbors and grid distance computation
- **bmu.R**: Best Matching Unit finding with support for complete and NA-aware distance metrics
- **batch_update.R**: Batch weight updates using Gaussian neighborhood kernel with NA handling per dimension
- **growth.R**: Error accumulation, distribution from non-boundary to boundary neurons, directed growth candidate selection, and neuron insertion

### Distance and Neighborhood Functions
- **distance.R**: Euclidean distance computations (squared and standard), NA-aware scaling, and pairwise distance matrices
- **neighborhood.R**: Gaussian neighborhood kernel and linear sigma decay scheduling
- **nan_handling.R**: Per-dimension missingness rates, weighted distance metrics, and neighbor-based imputation for poorly-observed dimensions

### Quality Assessment and Clustering
- **metrics.R**: Topographic error, quantization error, and clustering evaluation metrics (purity, NMI, ARI)
- **clustering.R**: Vesanto-Alhoniemi two-level clustering using Ward's hierarchical or K-means with automatic k selection via Davies-Bouldin or silhouette scores
- **plotting.R**: U-matrix computation, component planes, hit counts, and topology edge extraction for visualization

### Data Preprocessing
- **pooled.R**: Pooled cross-sectional data preparation with optional z-score normalization and metadata preservation
- **utils.R**: Position key management, neuron structure creation, and data format conversions

### Testing and Examples
- **tests/testthat/test_dbgsom.R**: Comprehensive test suite covering utilities, topology, distance, neighborhood, growth thresholds, core training, NA handling, clustering, and metrics
- **run_tests.R**: Standalone test runner for environments without testthat
- **examples/example_iris_r.R**: Complete workflow demonstration on iris dataset including training, metrics, clustering, and evaluation

### Package Configuration
- **DESCRIPTION**: Package metadata with dependencies
- **NAMESPACE**: Exported functions for public API
- **tests/testthat.R**: Test harness configuration

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Two-phase training**: Coarse phase with growth and large neighborhood, fine phase without growth and small neighborhood for refinement
- **Directed growth**: Considers 1st and 2nd-order neighbors to bias growth toward high-error regions
- **NA handling**: Per-dimension observation weights and scaling to handle missing values without imputation during training
- **Hexagonal topology**: Odd-r offset coordinate system with cube coordinate conversion for efficient distance computation
- **Growth threshold methods**: Supports both spreading factor (parameter-based) and statistical error (data-driven) approaches
- **Automatic k selection**: Davies-Bouldin and silhouette-based methods for optimal cluster number determination

author: dnslmnv
body:
### Motivation
- Admin users could not add product characteristics (attribute values) conveniently from the product edit page, and inline choices could produce mismatched category/attribute pairs. 
- The catalog filtering API parsed attribute filters but lacked numeric-range support and duplicated logic between endpoints. 
- The frontend catalog UI didn't expose numeric range inputs and did not support single-choice (select) attribute behavior.

### Description
- Add full admin support for characteristics by registering `CategoryAttribute` and `ProductAttributeValue`, adding a `ProductAttributeValueInline` on the `Product` admin, and restricting inline attribute choices to the product's category; add inline form validation to prevent assigning attributes from a different category (changes in `backend/catalog/admin.py`).
- Refactor attribute filtering into a shared helper `_apply_attribute_filters` and extend it to support numeric range syntax `attribute=<id>:<min>..<max>` while keeping boolean, string and exact-number matching (changes in `backend/api/views.py`).
- Add a unit test covering numeric-range attribute filtering to the product API tests (`backend/api/tests.py`).
- Update frontend catalog code to surface numeric range inputs and single-choice (`select`) behavior, wire range inputs into query param building (frontend changes in `frontend/src/App.tsx` and `frontend/src/components/CatalogPage.tsx`).

### Testing
- Ran backend tests with `cd backend && python manage.py test api.tests` and all tests passed (`OK`, 18 tests ran).
- Built the frontend with `cd frontend && npm run build` and the production build completed successfully.
- Started the dev frontend (`vite`) to capture a screenshot; Vite logged proxy connection errors because the local backend API was not running, which is an environment issue and not a code regression.

author: copilot
body:
Preview continues showing old featured image when changed but not published. Root cause: code listened for clicks on `#set-post-thumbnail` (opens media modal) rather than actual image selection.

## Changes

- **Replace click listeners with MutationObserver** in `assets/js/admin.js` and `assets/js/elementor.js`
  - Observes `#postimagediv` for DOM mutations (child/attribute changes)
  - Detects when WordPress actually sets/removes/changes featured image
  - Debounced 1s refresh ensures thumbnail ID persists before preview update

**Before:**
```javascript
$(document).on('click', '#set-post-thumbnail', function() {
    setTimeout(refreshPreview, 500);  // Triggers when modal opens, not when image set
});
```

**After:**
```javascript
new MutationObserver(function(mutations) {
    clearTimeout(refreshTimeout);
    refreshTimeout = setTimeout(refreshPreview, 1000);
}).observe(postImageDiv, {
    childList: true,
    subtree: true,
    attributes: true,
    attributeFilter: ['class']
});
```

Handles all cases: initial set, change, and removal of featured images in both Classic/Gutenberg and Elementor editors.

author: m4nt0de4
body:
## Summary

Claude Code's `Write`/`Edit` tools use `fs.writeFile()` internally — they do **not** shell-expand `~`. When the AI follows markdown instructions containing `~/.claude/...` paths and passes them to `Write`/`Edit` tools, a literal directory named `~` is created in the current working directory instead of writing to the user's home directory.

This PR fixes **11 files** across v3.0 where Write-facing markdown instructions used `~/.claude/` shorthand, replacing them with `$HOME/.claude/` (with resolution notes where appropriate).

**Root cause:** The PAI system has two path systems:
- **TypeScript tools** (`paths.ts`, hooks) — use `homedir()` + `join()` → **correct**, unaffected
- **Markdown instructions** — use `~/.claude/` shorthand that the AI passes verbatim to `Write`/`Edit` → **broken on all platforms**

This is platform-agnostic — affects Linux, macOS, and WSL equally since `Write`/`Edit` are API-level file operations, not shell commands.

## Files Changed (11 files, 20 insertions, 18 deletions)

| File | Lines | Change |
|------|-------|--------|
| `PAI/Components/Algorithm/v1.6.0.md` | 287, 664 | PRD creation path + PATH RULE warning |
| `PAI/SKILL.md` | 326, 703 | Same (built version of Algorithm) |
| `WorldThreatModelHarness/Workflows/UpdateModels.md` | 82, 86 | Save/write model paths |
| `WorldThreatModelHarness/SKILL.md` | 42 | Model storage reference |
| `Evals/Workflows/CreateUseCase.md` | 42, 100, 124, 176 | 4× Create file instructions |
| `Evals/Workflows/CreateJudge.md` | 36 | Create judge config |
| `Evals/Workflows/CompareModels.md` | 49 | Create comparison config |
| `Evals/Workflows/ComparePrompts.md` | 79 | Create comparison config |
| `Research/Workflows/ExtractAlpha.md` | 382, 385 | Scratch workspace + history paths |
| `Agents/AgentProfileSystem.md` | 184 | Agent profile creation |
| `PAI/THEHOOKSYSTEM.md` | 163 | Ratings write path |

## What Was NOT Changed

- **Shell commands** (`mkdir -p ~/.claude/...` in bash blocks) — shell correctly expands `~`
- **Read-only references** (`Read ~/.claude/...`) — Read tool handles `~` correctly
- **TypeScript code** — already uses `homedir()` + `join()` via `paths.ts`
- **User-facing documentation** — `~` is fine in human-readable contexts

## Testing

```bash
# Verify no Write-facing tilde paths remain in v3.0 skills:
cd Releases/v3.0/.claude/skills
grep -rn '~/.claude/' --include='*.md' | grep -iE '(create|write|save|work in)' | grep -v '```bash' | grep -v 'mkdir'
# Should return 0 results
```

- Relates to #699 (tilde path expansion in `plansDirectory` setting)

body:
### Motivation
- Production `.env` generation was producing files with unresolved placeholders (literal `${...}` or `__PLACEHOLDER__`) which caused Docker Compose warnings and PostgreSQL role interpolation errors during startup. 
- Persisting a bcrypt password hash into `generated_secrets.env` exposed `$`-style fragments that Docker Compose tried to treat as environment variable names, creating noisy warnings and potential runtime interpolation issues. 

### Description
- Updated `.env.production.template` and `.env.local.template` to use `envsubst`-compatible placeholders (`${...}`) so templates render to concrete values instead of leaving literal placeholders. 
- Changed `bootstrap.sh` to detect unresolved placeholders in an existing target env file and regenerate it (without requiring `--force`) rather than silently skipping, and kept the `envsubst` rendering step. 
- Removed writing `ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH` into `generated_secrets.env` in `deploy.sh` and instead derive the bcrypt hash at runtime inside the backend seeding step so Docker Compose no longer sees raw `$...` hash fragments. 
- Adjusted admin seeding code in `deploy.sh` to read `ADMIN_PASSWORD` and compute `hashed = hash_password(password)` inside the container before inserting/updating the admin user. 

### Testing
- Performed a syntax check of modified scripts with `bash -n bootstrap.sh deploy.sh`, which succeeded. 
- Rendered `.env.production.template` with a representative `generated_secrets.env` and `envsubst` and verified no unresolved placeholders remained using `rg` (test command shown in validation), which passed. 
- Ran the repository `git` operations to commit the changes and created the PR; automated checks used in the rollout showed successful commits and diffs.

author: parul-gupta29
body:
Three issues caused the Phase 2 loss to oscillate without converging:

1. No learning rate warmup — freshly initialised LoRA parameters received full LR (3e-5) from step 1, destabilising the already-trained output heads and hierarchy embedding. Added 1000-step linear warmup + cosine decay (matching the Phase 1 scheduler pattern).

2. No learning rate decay — the constant LR prevented the optimiser from settling into a minimum. Now decays via cosine schedule to 1e-6.

3. Unclamped ELBO loss weights — the per-level weight ≈ 1/t diverges as t → sampling_eps (≈1e-3), producing weights up to ~1000x. With the small effective batch size of 16, these spikes caused high-variance loss oscillation. Clamped expm1 denominator to 1e-4 floor.

author: jpotoff
body: This PR adds support for tabulated potentials using the potential file format similar (but not identical) to NAMD. Users can access the tabulated potentials by setting "Potential = TABULATED" in the GOMC control file. Tabulated potentials should not be used with long range corrections. Includes the ability to use linear or cubic interpolation between table data points. The tabulated potentials are slower than using an analytical potential. Using a table data spacing of 0.01 and cubic interpolation, it was possible to reproduce the Lennard-Jones energy generated with the full LJ potential to 7 decimal places. GEMC simulations were performed on TraPPE-UA ethane, butane and decane and OPC water. The resulting saturated liquid densities agree with simulations of the analytical LJ potential to within 0.5% (many cases agreement to within 0.2% was achieved). Differences in the gas phase densities of 1-2% were observed. When plotted on a typical phase diagram, it is difficult to see any difference in the results.

body:
## Summary

Replace assertion statements with explicit `ValueError` exceptions in production code. Assertions are disabled when Python runs with `-O` optimizations, which can silently skip critical validation checks.

## Changes

- **Replace 4 assert statements with ValueError** in agent execution code
- **Remove unnecessary pass statements** from abstract methods  
- **Clean up commented-out code** (dead code)

## Why This Matters

When Python runs with optimization flags (`python -O` or `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1`), all `assert` statements are removed from the bytecode. This means critical validation checks would be silently bypassed in production deployments that use optimizations.

## Files Modified

- `src/nodetool/agents/agent.py`: workspace, docker_image, task validation

**Core documentation:**
- `README.md` - Product overview, installation (Windows/MacOS), default key mappings, customization basics
- `QUICK_START.md` - Fast-track setup for new users
- `TROUBLESHOOTING.md` - Hardware/software/OS-specific issues (antivirus false positives, permissions, connectivity)

**Reference documentation:**
- `USE_CASES.md` - 40+ configuration examples across 8 workflows (gaming, video editing, development, streaming, etc.)
- `FAQ.md` - Common questions on compatibility, programming, hardware specs
- `DOCUMENTATION.md` - Navigation guide linking all resources

**Repository maintenance:**
- `.gitignore` - Excludes OS artifacts, temp files, IDE configs

## Key Content

**Installation guidance** addresses common blockers:
- Windows Defender SmartScreen bypass
- MacOS Gatekeeper permissions
- Antivirus false positive handling

**Default mappings documented:**
- Keys 1-4: Arrow keys (↑↓←→)

author: copilot
body:
## Describe your changes

Added standard entry point fields to package.json for improved module resolution:

- **`main`**: `src/gameinput.js` - primary entry point
- **`module`**: `src/gameinput.js` - ESM indicator for bundlers
- **`exports`**: explicit module graph
  - `.` → main module
  - `./schema` → schema submodule
  - `./models` → models submodule

Both `main` and `module` point to the same file because this is an ESM-only package (`"type": "module"`). Modern bundlers prefer `exports`; the other fields provide fallback compatibility.

**Usage:**
```js
// Main module
import { GameInput } from "gameinputjs"

// Submodules
import { GameInputSchema } from "gameinputjs/schema"
import { GameInputModels } from "gameinputjs/models"
```

## Describe your testing

- All 2095 existing tests pass
- Verified module resolution for all export paths
- Confirmed ESM import compatibility in Node.js

> The `package.json` does not specify `main`, `module`, or `exports` entrypoints. This reduces compatibility with bundlers and Node-style imports.
>

> ```json
> {
>   "name": "gameinputjs",

>     "./schema": "./src/gameinput-schema.js",
>     "./models": "./src/gameinput-models.js"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> ## Benefits
> - Better compatibility with bundlers (Webpack, Rollup, Vite, etc.)
> - Proper module resolution in Node.js
> - Allows importing sub-modules directly
> - Follows modern package.json conventions

author: ovsh
body:
## Summary
Improved the reliability of opening the Skills window by switching from a notification-based approach to directly accessing and managing the window through NSApp.windows. This resolves issues where the notification handler in MenuView was unreliable due to MenuBarExtra popover lifecycle constraints.

## Key Changes
- **AppEntry.swift**: Enhanced `showSkillsWindow()` to search for and bring the Skills window to front directly by iterating through `NSApp.windows` and matching on window identifier or title
- **AppEntry.swift**: Added fallback notification posting for initial app launch before SwiftUI has created the window
- **MenuView.swift**: Removed the unreliable `onReceive` notification handler that was attempting to open the window via `openWindow(id:)`

## Implementation Details
The new approach addresses a fundamental issue: MenuView lives inside a MenuBarExtra popover that is only active when visible, making notification-based window management unreliable. By directly accessing the window from the app delegate, we can reliably bring the Skills window to front regardless of the current UI state. The fallback notification ensures the window can still be opened on initial launch before SwiftUI has created it.

body:
Adds commands for taking calibration frames during observatory setup.

## Commands

**`pocs camera take-bias`** - Takes bias frames with zero exposure, stacks to master bias, reports sigma-clipped statistics
- Default: 10 frames to `/home/panoptes/images/bias`
- Options: `--num-images`, `--output-dir`, `--convert`, `--verbose`

**`pocs run take-flats`** - Takes flat fields with automatic exposure adjustment  
- Slews to altitude/azimuth (defaults: 70°, 180° opposite sun)
- Validates `--which` parameter (evening/morning only)
- Options: `--alt`, `--az`, `--min/max-counts`, `--target-adu`, exposure controls, `--no-tracking`

## Usage

```bash
# Quick bias calibration
pocs camera take-bias -n 20

# Evening flats with defaults
pocs run take-flats

# Morning flats at custom position  
pocs run take-flats --which morning --alt 45 --az 270
```

## Changes

- Added `take_bias_cmd()` in `cli/camera.py` with bias stacking pipeline
- Added `run_take_flats()` in `cli/run.py` calling `Observatory.take_flat_fields()`
- Added `validate_which()` callback for parameter validation
- Updated `cli-guide.md` with both commands
- Updated `CHANGELOG.md` unreleased section

Implements promptfile for generating hierarchical outlines from VTI/VTT transcript files with section durations and statistics.

## Implementation

- **Promptfile**: `.github/copilot/Promptfiles/summarize-vti-content.prompt.md`
  - Dual format detection: VTI (markdown-structured) and VTT (WebVTT timestamps)
  - Single `vti_file` string argument for file path
  - Hierarchical outline generation with duration extraction
  - Statistical analysis (total/average/longest/shortest sections)

- **Test artifact**: `past-class-recordings/2026-02/AI-Assisted Software Development with GitHub Copilot (Wed Morning).vtt`
  - Valid WebVTT format with realistic training content (3 sections, 2:35 duration)

- **Documentation**: Usage guide and directory README

## Usage

```
@summarize-vti-content vti_file="past-class-recordings/2026-02/AI-Assisted Software Development with GitHub Copilot (Wed Morning).vtt"
```

## Format Handling

**VTI**: Extracts durations from markdown headings `## Section (MM:SS)`

**VTT**: Calculates durations from timestamp ranges `HH:MM:SS.mmm --> HH:MM:SS.mmm`, groups consecutive captions into logical sections

## Output Structure

- Document overview (source, format, total duration, section count)
- Detailed hierarchical outline with subsections and key points
- Summary statistics (section counts, duration analysis)

author: wu-tian807
body:
## Problem

`limitHistoryTurns()` can orphan `toolResult` messages by removing the preceding `assistant` message that contained the matching `tool_calls`. The code already documents this — `attempt.ts` lines 671-673:

```
// Re-run tool_use/tool_result pairing repair after truncation, since
// limitHistoryTurns can orphan tool_result blocks by removing the
// assistant message that contained the matching tool_use.
```

The subsequent repair step (`sanitizeToolUseResultPairing`) handles this correctly, but `repairToolUseResultPairing` is disabled for OpenAI in `transcript-policy.ts`:

```typescript
repairToolUseResultPairing: !isOpenAi && repairToolUseResultPairing,
```

OpenAI's Chat Completions API is the strictest about tool pairing — it rejects orphaned `toolResult` messages with `400 Invalid parameter: messages with role 'tool' must be a response to a preceding message with 'tool_calls'`. Once this happens, the session enters a death loop: retry → same truncated history → same 400 → retry.

Note: this does **not** affect the OpenAI Responses API (`openai-responses`, `openai-codex-responses`), which is stateful and manages tool pairing server-side.

### Reproduction paths

1. **Pure OpenAI single-provider:** Session accumulates many tool calls → `limitHistoryTurns` truncates and orphans a `toolResult` → repair skipped → 400 error.

2. **Cross-provider heartbeat:** Upstream natively supports `heartbeat.model` with a different provider (e.g. Anthropic heartbeat, OpenAI primary). Heartbeat produces `tool_calls` in the shared session → truncation orphans a `toolResult` → primary model (OpenAI) picks up the session → repair skipped → 400 error.

## Fix

```typescript
// New: distinguish stateful Responses API from stateless Chat Completions
const isOpenAiResponsesApi =
  params.modelApi === "openai-responses" || params.modelApi === "openai-codex-responses";

// Before:
repairToolUseResultPairing: !isOpenAi && repairToolUseResultPairing,
// After:
repairToolUseResultPairing: repairToolUseResultPairing || (isOpenAi && !isOpenAiResponsesApi),
```

This enables the existing, already-tested `repairToolUseResultPairing()` function for OpenAI Chat Completions models. The function only drops orphaned `toolResult` messages and synthesizes placeholder results for missing `toolResult` — both safe operations that align with OpenAI's strict message format requirements.

**Behavior change by provider:**
- Google / Anthropic: unchanged (`true || false` = `true`)
- **OpenAI Chat Completions (`openai`, `openai-completions`): `false` → `true`** (fix)
- OpenAI Responses API (`openai-responses`, `openai-codex-responses`): unchanged (`false`)
- Other providers: unchanged (`false || false` = `false`)

## Test plan

- [x] Added 4 regression tests verifying `repairToolUseResultPairing` is enabled for OpenAI Chat Completions, disabled for OpenAI Responses API, enabled for Anthropic, enabled for Google
- [x] `vitest run src/agents/transcript-policy.test.ts` — 8 tests pass
- [x] `vitest run src/agents/pi-embedded-runner.sanitize-session-history.test.ts` — passes (including "does not synthesize tool results for openai-responses")
- [x] `pnpm tsgo --noEmit` — type check passes
- [x] `pnpm format` — formatted with project oxfmt

### Changes (2 files, +44 -1)

- `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts` — Add `isOpenAiResponsesApi` guard, enable repair for OpenAI Chat Completions
- `src/agents/transcript-policy.test.ts` — 4 regression tests

body:
Also use `zlib-ng-compat` on Linux

---

Checksum change is due to project move from Datastax to Apache which included a repository name change:
- https://github.com/apache/cassandra-cpp-driver/commit/6bc16491bfb418fe9f16c9228ae0918d40262edf
- https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CASSCPP-1

The difference happens as `git archive` uses repo name as top directory in tarball so prepending `cassandra-` to repo name causes checksum mismatch.

This can be verified by comparing with copy from FreeBSD - https://pkg.freebsd.org/ports-distfiles/datastax-cpp-driver-2.17.1_GH0.tar.gz
```console
❯ curl -sL https://pkg.freebsd.org/ports-distfiles/datastax-cpp-driver-2.17.1_GH0.tar.gz | sha256
53b4123aad59b39f2da0eb0ce7fe0e92559f7bba0770b2e958254f17bffcd7cf

❯ curl -sL https://pkg.freebsd.org/ports-distfiles/datastax-cpp-driver-2.17.1_GH0.tar.gz | tar zx

❯ curl -sL https://github.com/apache/cassandra-cpp-driver/archive/refs/tags/2.17.1.tar.gz | sha256
e6ab5f5c60a916dd6c0dd9a19a883a4a1ab3d6b4e95cab925a186fecff08344e

❯ curl -sL https://github.com/apache/cassandra-cpp-driver/archive/refs/tags/2.17.1.tar.gz | tar zx

❯ diffoscope cpp-driver-2.17.1/ cassandra-cpp-driver-2.17.1/

❯ echo $?
0
```

Contents/metadata of extracted files are identical. Only issue is the first directory name
* cpp-driver-2.17.1/
* cassandra-cpp-driver-2.17.1/

author: sanity
body:
## Problem

CI currently takes ~14-18 min on success and ~25-35 min with retries. The `|| retry` pattern re-runs the **entire workspace** when any single test fails, adding 10-15 min penalty. Additionally, all 45 `#[freenet_test]` tests use fixed sleep waits (10-40s each) instead of polling for actual node readiness.

## Solution

### 1. cargo-nextest with per-test retries

Replace `cargo test ... || retry` with `cargo nextest run --profile ci`. The `.config/nextest.toml` CI profile configures:
- **2 retries per failed test** (not the whole workspace)
- `fail-fast = false` to surface multiple issues
- `slow-timeout` at 120s with terminate-after to catch hangs

This reduces retry penalty from 10-15 min to 30-60s.

### 2. health_check_readiness on all tests

Enable `health_check_readiness = true` on all 45 `#[freenet_test]` invocations across 6 test files. This polls `wait_for_all_nodes_ready()` instead of sleeping fixed durations. Nodes typically become ready in 2-5s on localhost; current fixed waits are 10-40s per test.

**Files changed:**
- `operations.rs` — 18 tests
- `test_macro_example.rs` — 9 tests
- `edge_case_state_sizes.rs` — 6 tests
- `connectivity.rs` — 4 tests
- `error_notification.rs` — 4 tests
- `isolated_node_regression.rs` — 4 tests

## Testing

- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets` passes
- [x] `cargo fmt` clean
- [ ] CI passes with nextest

## Summary

- What changed:
  - Units now have explicit server-authoritative status (`OFFLINE`, `AVAILABLE`, `IN TRANSIT`, `ON SCENE`) replicated via `ARC_pub_unitStatuses`.
  - Incident acceptance is now gated: a group must be `AVAILABLE` before `ARC_fnc_tocRequestAcceptIncident` will accept.
  - OPS secondary action (pre-acceptance) toggles group status `AVAILABLE`/`OFFLINE` through server request flow.
  - Status transitions are automated through lifecycle:
    - accept incident → `IN TRANSIT`
    - incident marked close-ready → `ON SCENE`
    - incident close → `AVAILABLE`
  - TOC now has persistent visibility of all unit statuses in CMD tab; OPS details show current group status and acceptance gating state.
  - **Example (server gate):**
    ```sqf
    private _statusNow = if (_statusIdx < 0) then { "OFFLINE" } else { toUpper (trim ((_unitStatuses # _statusIdx) # 1)) };
    if (_statusNow isNotEqualTo "AVAILABLE") exitWith
    {
        ["Incident acceptance denied: your group must set status to AVAILABLE first."] remoteExec ["ARC_fnc_clientHint", owner _caller];
        false
    };
    ```

body:
## Summary
This PR improves the reliability and user experience of async operations by adding distributed locks to prevent concurrent task execution and enhancing polling mechanisms across the frontend with better timeout handling and status feedback.

## Key Changes

### Backend (Celery Tasks)
- **Distributed Locks**: Added Redis-based lease locks to `sync_account_data` and `parse_single_chat` tasks to prevent multiple concurrent executions of the same task
  - Locks are acquired with `nx=True` (only set if not exists) and auto-expire after task timeout
  - Tasks return early if another instance is already running, with appropriate logging
  - Locks are cleaned up in `finally` blocks to ensure proper release

### Frontend - AccountChats
- **Improved Polling**: Changed from `setTimeout` (one-time) to `setInterval` (recurring) for chat parsing status checks
  - Polls every 5 seconds instead of waiting 10 seconds before first check
  - Added 5-minute timeout with user-facing warning message when parsing takes longer than expected
  - Tracks polling start times per chat to enforce timeout limits
  - Added `parsingTimeoutChats` state to display timeout warning UI
  - Better cleanup of polling timers and tracking maps on unmount

### Frontend - Contacts
- **Refactor**: Extracted load logic into `useCallback` for better reusability
- **Manual Refresh**: Added refresh button with loading state to manually refetch contact summary data
- Improved error state handling

### Frontend - InviteCampaigns
- **Auto-polling**: Added automatic polling of campaign list every 5 seconds when any campaign is active
- **Detail Polling**: Added separate polling for campaign detail view when open
- Both polling mechanisms respect component lifecycle and clean up properly

### Infrastructure (docker-compose.prod.yml)
- **Celery Beat Health**: Added health check for celery beat service
- **Dependencies**: Added explicit service dependencies (db, backend) with proper conditions
- Ensures beat scheduler starts only after required services are healthy

## Implementation Details
- All polling uses 5-second intervals for consistent UX
- Polling automatically stops when no longer needed (no active campaigns, chat parsing complete)
- Timeout warnings provide user feedback for long-running operations
- Redis locks use task IDs to track which task holds the lock, enabling better debugging

author: maddyli
body:
A Medplum user ran into an issue with the Smart on FHIR launch, which would have been avoided if project-scoped User resources are also deleted when the ProjectMembership is deleted upon user removal. 

They had added project-scoped users to their project, and then deleted those users using the "Remove user" button in the UI. This resulted in the ProjectMembership being deleted, but the User resources still exists as (as Users in that `project`) without a ProjectMembership attached. 

Then, they re-added these users, with the same emails, as server-scoped users. Upon attempting to oauth in the middle of the Smart on FHIR launch, Medplum server would look up User resources attached to that email, find the User that does not have a ProjectMembership attached (the User that we first provisioned), and it does not allow the users to log in. We were able to resolve this by deleting all the Users without a ProjectMembership attached. 

This PR aims to ensure that we don't have hanging project-scoped User resources without a ProjectMembership resource attached.

💡 What: 
1. Removed a hardcoded 600ms `setTimeout` in the attack simulation flow.

<!-- DO NOT MODIFY OR DELETE THIS TEMPLATE. IT IS USED IN AUTOMATION. -->

# Bug

<!-- If this is an engineering change or test change only, you do not need an issue. -->
<!-- Find or create an issue in NuGet/Home and paste the full url. -->
<!-- At the maintainers discretion, multiple changes may apply to a single issue, but only when the PRs are all created within a short period of time. -->
Fixes: https://github.com/NuGet/Home/issues/12552

## Description

When `--no-restore` is passed to `dotnet add package` in a CPM-enabled project, the command writes a versioned `<PackageReference Version="...">` directly to the .csproj, ignoring Central Package Management. This happens because CPM detection relies on the `DependencyGraphSpec` built during restore, which `--no-restore` skips. The result is NU1008 on the next restore.

This fix adds a new `IsCentralPackageManagementEnabled()` method to `MSBuildAPIUtility` that checks the MSBuild-evaluated `ManagePackageVersionsCentrally` property (available via `GetProject()` without restore), and sets `VersionCentrallyManaged` on the `LibraryDependency` in the `--no-restore` path. The existing downstream CPM handling then correctly produces a versionless `<PackageReference>` in the .csproj and a `<PackageVersion>` in `Directory.Packages.props`.

- [x] Meaningful title, helpful description and a linked NuGet/Home issue
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Link to an issue or pull request to update docs if this PR changes settings, environment variables, new feature, etc.

author: gaborbernat
body:
When a child environment inherits `set_env` via cross-section substitution (e.g., `set_env = {[testenv]set_env}`), environment variables like `PYTHONHASHSEED` were silently replaced with their auto-generated defaults. This meant explicitly setting `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` in the base environment had no effect in child environments that referenced it — the child would always get a random hash seed. 🐛

The root cause is a timing issue: tox applies default environment variables (including `PYTHONHASHSEED`) during post-processing, before the `{[testenv]...}` substitution is expanded. Since the unexpanded reference is not yet in the raw config dict, the defaults are materialized first. When the substitution later expands and populates the raw dict, the already-materialized default takes precedence during lookup.

The fix ensures that when a deferred substitution is expanded, any previously materialized defaults for the same keys are evicted, allowing the explicitly configured values to take priority as intended.

Fixes #2872.

author: divens
body:
## Summary

  Add all Windows-specific runtime code on top of the cross-platform abstractions established in PRs 01–07. This branch brings zellij to a functional state on
  Windows.

##  Changes

  **Signal and process control**
  - AsyncSignalListener (Windows): polls crossterm::terminal::size() at 100ms for resize events, tokio::signal::windows::{ctrl_c, ctrl_break, ctrl_close} for quit
  - BlockingSignalIterator (Windows): SetConsoleCtrlHandler + AtomicBool, polls terminal size at 50ms
  - signal_process (Windows): GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent for Interrupt, TerminateProcess for Kill/HangUp
  - Fallback gates narrowed from cfg(not(unix)) to cfg(not(any(unix, windows)))

  **IPC with named pipes**
  - ipc_connect/ipc_bind/ipc_bind_async helpers with cfg(windows) gates using GenericNamespaced named pipes
  - Dual-pipe architecture: separate main + reply pipe per connection to work around half-duplex named pipe limitation
  - Marker files created alongside named pipes for session discovery (is_ipc_socket returns is_file() on non-Unix)
  - assert_socket split: Unix probes with ConnStatus; non-Unix returns true to avoid deadlocking the server accept loop
  - Web server IPC: replaced tokio::net::UnixListener/UnixStream with interprocess::local_socket::tokio for cross-platform support

  **Client input and server spawn**
  - Two-mode Windows input strategy: crossterm::event::read() for native console (Windows Terminal, cmd.exe), termwiz byte parser for terminal emulators (Alacritty,
  etc.) via ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT
  - cast_crossterm_key: converts crossterm::event::KeyEvent to KeyWithModifier with Ctrl/Alt byte synthesis
  - spawn_server: CREATE_NO_WINDOW | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP flags on Windows
  - 8MB stack trampoline in main() for Windows (default 1MB overflows during WASM compilation)
  - 8MB stack for plugin executor and server worker threads
  - Skip ANSI terminal query on Windows to unblock startup

  **Cross-platform test fixes**
  - Socket tests: IpcGuard/IpcName type aliases with GenericNamespaced on Windows vs GenericFilePath/TempDir on Unix
  - Layout snapshot tests: normalize_layout_debug() normalizes path separators on Windows
  - Setup tests: PathBuf::join + display() instead of hardcoded / separators
  - Server OS tests: cross-platform command helpers (long_running_cmd, echo_cmd, stdin_reader_cmd) with CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows
  - ConPTY diagnostic reproduction example for 0xc0000142

  **CI**
  - New build-windows job: cargo check --no-default-features on windows-latest
  - New test-windows job: runs zellij-utils, zellij-server, zellij-client tests on Windows
  - Manual workflow_dispatch trigger enabled

# feat: GYEOL Gateway 서버 + Koyeb 배포 설정

## Summary

Adds a lightweight FastAPI gateway server (`server/`) as a replacement for the heavy OpenClaw Docker image, and fixes the existing `openclaw-deploy/` configuration.

**New: `server/`** — Standalone FastAPI backend that:
- Proxies `/api/chat` requests to Groq API (llama-3.3-70b-versatile)
- Exposes `/webhook/telegram` for Telegram bot integration
- Strips markdown formatting from AI responses
- Includes Dockerfile for container deployment on Koyeb

**Fixed: `openclaw-deploy/`** — For the original OpenClaw image:
- Removed invalid `moltbook` channel from `openclaw.json` (caused startup crash)
- Added `entrypoint-wrapper.sh` to patch nginx config at runtime, removing the browser sidecar proxy block that causes `host not found in upstream "browser"` errors in containerized environments

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Telegram webhook bug**: `telegram_webhook()` calls `await chat(request)` passing the raw Telegram webhook request. The `chat()` handler then calls `request.json()` which re-parses the Telegram payload — `body.get("message")` will return the Telegram message *object* (not a string), so chat will likely fail silently and always hit the exception fallback. This needs to be refactored to construct a proper chat payload.
- [ ] **No authentication on `/api/chat`**: The endpoint is publicly accessible with no token/key validation. Anyone who discovers the URL can consume your Groq API quota. The `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` from the original plan is not implemented.
- [ ] **Ephemeral Docker registry**: The image was pushed to `ttl.sh/gyeol-gateway-2026:2h` which expires after 2 hours. If Koyeb needs to re-pull the image (scaling, redeployment, instance migration), it will fail. Move to a persistent registry (GHCR, Docker Hub) before relying on this in production.
- [ ] **Unused import**: `import json` in `main.py` is not used.
- [ ] **Verify Vercel env var `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL`** is updated to point to the Koyeb service URL, and that the frontend chat route (`app/api/chat/route.ts`) correctly calls the gateway's `/api/chat` endpoint.

### Test Plan
1. `curl https://<koyeb-url>/health` → expect `{"ok": true, ...}`
2. `curl -X POST https://<koyeb-url>/api/chat -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"message":"안녕","agentId":"test"}'` → expect Korean AI response
3. Send a message to `@ai_gyeol_bot` on Telegram → likely hits the fallback error path due to the webhook bug above; verify and fix

### Notes
- The `entrypoint-wrapper.sh` sed replacement is fragile — if upstream OpenClaw changes how nginx config is generated, the patch may silently stop working.
- Markdown stripping (`content.replace("*", "")...`) is aggressive and will remove legitimate asterisks from content.

author: mdelrosa
body:
# Upgrade openapi-python-client (0.16.0 → 0.28.2) and fix cascading SDK changes

## Problem

Our backend upgraded **pydantic** (^1.10.12 → 2.12.5), **fastapi** (0.99.1 → 0.119.0), and **litellm** (>=1.29.5,<=1.39.5 → 1.75.3). These upgrades changed how the backend's OpenAPI spec (`openapi.json`) is generated — most notably, Pydantic v2 emits `anyOf: [{type}, {type: null}]` for `Optional[T]` fields instead of a simple `nullable: true` annotation. This broke our existing `openapi-python-client` (0.16.0) stub generation pipeline, which could not parse the new nullable patterns.

## Solution

Rather than downgrading the backend or manually patching the spec by hand each time, we:

1. **Upgraded `openapi-python-client`** from 0.16.0 to 0.28.2, which has better support for modern OpenAPI patterns.
2. **Added a preprocessing step** (`scripts/preprocess_openapi.py`) that normalizes the spec before generation — collapsing Pydantic v2's `anyOf` nullable patterns back to the `nullable: true` form that the generator handles cleanly, and marking optional (non-required) schema properties as nullable so the generated `from_dict` parsers handle `None` responses gracefully.
3. **Fixed all breaking changes** in the SDK wrapper layer (`src/okareo/`) caused by the generator upgrade's new conventions.

## Major Changes

### **`scripts/preprocess_openapi.py`** (new)
Preprocessing script run on `openapi.json` before generation. Two passes:
- **`collapse_nullable_anyof()`** — rewrites `anyOf: [{schema}, {type: null}]` into the single inner schema with `nullable: true`. Skips path/query parameters (which don't support `nullable`).
- **`mark_optional_properties_nullable()`** — for every schema, any property not listed in `required` gets `nullable: true` added, so the generator emits `_parse_*` functions that handle `None`. Properties with non-null defaults (e.g. `default: {}`) are skipped — the generator rejects `nullable` on fields whose default is not `None`.

### **`Makefile`**
- Added `spec/preprocess` target that runs the preprocessing script.
- `openapi/generate` now depends on `spec/preprocess`, so preprocessing runs automatically whether invoked directly (CI) or via `openapi/update` (dev). It also cleans both `src/okareo_api_client` and the stale `okareo-api-client` output directory.
- `openapi/update` depends on `spec/update openapi/generate` — fetch spec, then generate (which includes preprocessing).

### **`.github/workflows/verify_spec.yml`**
- Updated `pip install` from `openapi-python-client==0.16.0 click==8.2.1 typer==0.9.*` to `openapi-python-client==0.28.2` (transitive deps like `typer` are resolved automatically; the old pins conflicted with 0.28.2).
- The workflow runs `make openapi/generate`, which now includes the preprocessing step, so CI validation stays in sync with the dev pipeline.

### **`src/okareo/okareo.py`**
- Renamed all `json_body=`, `multipart_data=`, and `form_data=` keyword arguments to `body=` (generator 0.17.0+ unified these).
- Renamed `type=` to `type_=` in `ScenarioSetResponse(...)` construction (generator appends `_` to Python reserved words).

### **`src/okareo/model_under_test.py`**
- **`body=` rename** — same `json_body=` → `body=` change as above.
- **`type_=` rename** — `TestRunPayloadV2(type_=...)` and `EvaluationPayload(type_=...)`.
- **UUID serialization** — generated `from_dict` methods now construct `UUID()` objects instead of passing raw strings. All call sites that feed UUIDs into `from_dict` or use them as dict keys now call `str()` explicitly: `add_data_point`, `add_data_point_async`, `_add_model_invocation_for_scenario` (including batch path), and `Driver.to_dict`.
- **Simulation conversion** — `_get_test_run_payload` converts the SDK's `Simulation` object to `TestRunPayloadV2SimulationParams.from_dict(simulation_params.to_dict())` so the generated model receives its expected type rather than an arbitrary object.
- **Assertion update** — `_run_test_internal` changed `assert isinstance(scenario_id, str)` to `assert scenario_id is not None` since `scenario_id` is now a `UUID`.

### **`src/okareo/async_utils.py`**
- `json_body=` → `body=` (1 location).

### **`okareo_tests/test_client.py`**
- Added `MOCK_UUID = str(uuid.uuid4())` constant and replaced all fake IDs (e.g. `"test_scenario_id"`) with valid UUIDs so generated `from_dict` calls don't fail on `UUID()` construction.
- Changed `uuid.UUID(scenario_response.scenario_id)` assertion to `assert isinstance(scenario_response.scenario_id, uuid.UUID)` since the field is already a UUID object.

### **`okareo_tests/test_integration_model_under_test.py`**
- `json_body=` → `body=` (8 locations).

### **`okareo_tests/test_langchain.py`**
- Replaced fake IDs (`"id"`, `"my-project"`) in `get_mut_response()` with valid UUIDs. Added `MOCK_UUID` constant and `import uuid`.

### **`okareo_tests/test_litellm_logger.py`**
- Same `get_mut_response()` UUID fix as `test_langchain.py`.

### **`okareo_tests/test_model_under_test.py`**
- Replaced all fake IDs (`"1"`, `"scenario-id"`, `"test-run-item-id"`, etc.) in `get_mut_fixture()` and inline mock JSON with valid UUIDs via `MOCK_UUID` / `MOCK_UUID_2` constants.
- `assert isinstance(response.scenario_id, str)` → `assert isinstance(response.scenario_id, uuid.UUID)`.

### **`okareo_tests/test_model_under_test_async.py`**
- Replaced `"id": "1"` and `"project_id": "1"` in `get_mut_fixture()` with valid UUIDs.

### **`okareo_tests/test_scenarios.py`**
- `.type` → `.type_` across all 11 assertion sites (reserved word rename).
- `assert isinstance(create_scenario_set.scenario_id, str)` → `isinstance(..., (str, uuid.UUID))`.

### **`src/okareo/okareo.py`** (generation_schema fix)
- Added conversion in `generate_scenario_set()`: if `generation_schema` is a `BaseGenerationSchema` subclass (a class, not an instance), it is converted to `ScenarioSetGenerateGenerationSchema.from_dict(cls.to_dict())` before the request is sent. This fixes `"Object of type ModelMetaclass is not JSON serializable"` since the generated model only knows how to serialize its own type.

### **`src/okareo_api_client/`** (regenerated)
Fully regenerated from the preprocessed spec using `openapi-python-client` 0.28.2. Key differences from the previous generation: nullable fields now have `_parse_*` helper functions that handle `None`, UUID fields are parsed into `UUID` objects, and parameter naming follows the updated conventions.

## Minor changes

### **test_integration_multiturn.py**
Update Gemini model from `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-09-2025` to `gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview`

## Benefits

1. **Stays in sync with backend** — the SDK generation pipeline now works with Pydantic v2's OpenAPI output without manual spec edits.
2. **Robust nullable handling** — the preprocessing + generator upgrade means optional fields that come back as `null` from the API are parsed correctly instead of crashing in `from_dict`.
3. **Automated and repeatable** — `make openapi/update` (dev) and `make openapi/generate` (CI) both include preprocessing, so the pipeline is consistent everywhere.

## Testing

- Unit tests (`okareo_tests/test_client.py`) updated and passing.
- Integration tests (`okareo_tests/test_integration_model_under_test.py`) updated and passing.
- Clean generation with no errors (only expected warnings about missing `$ref` targets for schemas not included in the trimmed spec).

## Implementation Notes

**Preprocessing is required, not optional**
The generator alone cannot handle all the spec quirks. The `collapse_nullable_anyof` pass is essential because the generator does not fully support deeply nested `anyOf` nullable patterns. The `mark_optional_properties_nullable` pass is essential because the backend's spec does not consistently mark optional properties as nullable, but the API does return `null` for them.

author: adjordjevic-tt
body:
Closes https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-exalens/issues/886

Added `TensixState` structure and `get_tensix_state` function in lib to make easier to llk team to compare states.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces a new API that performs broad hardware register/debug-bus reads; correctness and stability depend on device-specific descriptions and the `l1_address`-gated read path, so subtle logic/availability issues can surface at runtime on some platforms.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new public `TensixState` dataclass and `get_tensix_state(device, location, l1_address=None)` helper in `tt_exalens_lib.py` to snapshot Tensix configuration registers (ALU/unpack/pack/ReLU/etc.), per-thread GPRs, and debug-bus-derived register-window/address counters into a single structured return value.
> 
> The API reads configuration registers via the block register store and optionally reads debug-bus signal groups atomically when an `l1_address` is provided (otherwise falling back to unsafe group reads), making it easier for external tooling to compare full Tensix state across runs.
>

author: calebporzio
body:
## Summary

- The callbacks in `Directives::get()` and `Directives::has()` had no return statement, implicitly returning `null`
- This `null` propagated through `BladeCompiler::compileStatements()` → `replaceFirstStatement()`, where `strlen(null)` evaluated to `0`, preventing the offset from advancing — causing an infinite loop during view compilation
- Fixed by adding `return '';` to both callbacks

## Test plan

- [x] Confirmed site hangs indefinitely on first load after `php artisan view:clear` without fix
- [x] Confirmed site loads in ~0.5s with fix applied

author: anthonytwh
body:
The Findings Severity Over Time chart on the overview page did not respond to provider type or account filters selected by the user. Two issues: 1. useState(initialData) only sets state on mount — when the SSR component re-renders with filtered data after a URL param change, the client component kept showing stale unfiltered data. Updated to use React's "set state during render" pattern to sync the data state synchronously when initialData changes, avoiding a flash of stale chart data. 2. handleTimeRangeChange called getSeverityTrendsByTimeRange without forwarding the active provider/account filter params from the URL. Now extracts filter[provider_type__in] and filter[provider_id__in] from searchParams and passes them to the server action. Additionally, overflow-hidden was removed from the ChartContainer in line-chart.tsx because it was clipping data points and line strokes at the top of the chart when values were at or near the Y-axis maximum. Recharts manages its own internal layout bounds so there is no risk of overflow into adjacent elements. The top margin was increased (10 → 20) for additional clearance, and padding={{ top: 20 }} was added to the YAxis to reserve space above the highest data point within the plot area, preventing clipping regardless of curve shape. ### Steps to review Please add a detailed description of how to review this PR. ### Checklist
